subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks — next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks — summary & next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of today's call:
- Scope: end-to-end inference for your customer-facing chat feature (avg. prompt 80 tokens, responses ~220 tokens).
- Primary goals: p95 latency < 250ms, p99 < 500ms; steady tokens/sec to support 120 concurrent sessions.
- Constraints: must run inside US region, must integrate with Globex SSO and existing VPC for Private deployment if needed.

What we tested (high level):
- Redwood hosted (opt. q4 quantized variant) vs Hyperscaler-managed endpoint (their standard inference API)
- A/B run: identical workload replay (same prompt set and seq len distribution) using your sample trace

Key results (attached full report):
- Redwood: p95 = 210ms, p99 = 460ms, sustained ~1,900 tokens/sec on 8-GPU pool (continuous batching + KV cache).
- Hyperscaler: p95 = 340ms, p99 = 790ms, sustained ~1,250 tokens/sec under same concurrency.
- Cost delta (approx): Redwood 22% lower cost per 1M tokens after batching/caching advantages.

Proposed next steps:
1) Run a focused A/B with your network team on a shorter 24-hour window — we confirm p95/p99 under your VPC egress and TLS setup (Rafael + Marissa).
2) Provide SOC2 evidence and architecture notes to your security team (Neha to lead).
3) If results match, schedule a pilot commit for Dedicated capacity and discuss SLA targets & pricing (Tom from procurement).

Can you confirm 24–26 Aug for the A/B window? I can loop in your infra lead and our solutions engineer (Marissa) and security (Neha).

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_latency_report.pdf, 20260812-globex-benchmarks.csv

Thanks Rafael — great write-up and impressive numbers. Quick notes from our side: 

- Appreciate the p95/p99 breakdown and the CSV trace. We'll validate with our infra team but initial read looks promising.
- 24–26 Aug works for the A/B window; I'll confirm exact start times once I sync with DevOps.
- Security will need the SOC2 paperwork and a short network diagram for the VPC setup (please send Neha any docs you have).

One ask: can Marissa include an apples-to-apples config comparison (instance types, model variant, batch size, KV cache settings) in the A/B run plan? The infra team wants exact parity.

Thanks,
Alice

alice.johnson@globex.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks — A/B config & plan

Hi Alice / Rafael —

I've sketched the A/B config to ensure parity. High level: 
- Workload: replay of provided trace (80 token prompts, 220 token responses mean).
- Model: open-model-v3 (quantized 4-bit) on both sides where possible; Hyperscaler run will use their best-effort similar variant — we'll note differences in the run log.
- Instance types: Redwood test uses 8xA10G-equivalent GPU pool with continuous batching enabled; Hyperscaler run uses their c-inference-16 type (not identical hardware; we'll note this in results).
- Batch config: target batch window 20ms, max batch size 64.
- KV cache: enabled for both; we'll warm with prefixes from your trace.
- Metrics: collect p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rates, GPU utilization, and tail latency histograms.

I'll attach the run manifest (a_b_test_config.yaml) and the exact command-lines we will run. Rafael — can Neha provide the SOC2 zip and network diagram to Alice after you get confirmation?

I'll plan to kick off the Redwood side at 00:00 UTC Aug 24 and coordinate the Hyperscaler run with Tom for synchronized start.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
